verses.zh: （大卫的训诲诗。）得赦免其过、遮盖其罪的，这人是有福的！
verses.en: By David; a well-written song.[NOTE:1] How blessed[NOTE:2] is the one whose rebellious acts are forgiven,[NOTE:3] whose sin is pardoned.[NOTE:4]
notes: Psalm 32. The psalmist recalls the agony he experienced prior to confessing his sins and affirms that true happiness comes when one’s sins are forgiven. He then urges others not to be stubborn, but to turn to God while forgiveness is available, for God extends his mercy to the repentant, while the wicked experience nothing but sorrow.

The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. The word is derived from a verb meaning “to be prudent; to be wise.” Various options are: “a contemplative song,” “a song imparting moral wisdom,” or “a skillful [i.e., well-written] song.” The term occurs in the superscriptions of Pss 32, 42, 44, 45, 52-55, 74, 78, 88, 89, and 142, as well as in Ps 47:7.

The Hebrew noun is an abstract plural. The word often refers metonymically to the happiness that God-given security and prosperity produce (see Pss 1:1, 3; 2:12; 34:9; 41:1; 65:4; 84:12; 89:15; 106:3; 112:1; 127:5; 128:1; 144:15). Here it refers to the relief that one experiences when one’s sins are forgiven.
Heb “lifted up.”
verses.commentary:
32:1 The term "blessed" (BDB 80, cf. Ps. 1:1), out of 45 times is used 26 times in Psalms, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT).
The theme is recurrent in Wisdom Literature and describes the faithful followers.

- Job 5:17; Ps. 94:12 – disciplined by Shaddai (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADDAI)

- Psalm 1:2 – studies and walks in God's word

- Psalm 2:12 – takes refuge in YHWH (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE)

- Psalm 32:1-2 – sin is forgiven

- Psalm 40:4; 84:12; Prov. 16:20 – trusts in YHWH

- Psalm 41:1-3; Prov. 14:21 – considers the poor

- Psalm 84:5 – strength is in YHWH

- Psalm 89:15 – know joy and walk in the light of YHWH's countenance

- Psalm 119:2 – seek Him with whole heart, observe His testimony (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)

- Psalm 112:1; 128:1 – fears YHWH, walks in His ways (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

- Psalm 146:5 – YHWH is his help

- Proverbs 3:13 – finds wisdom

- Proverbs 8:32,34 – listens to YHWH, keeps His ways

- Proverbs 28:14 – fears YHWH (see and
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR)

- Proverbs 29:18 – keeps YHWH's laws

The first two verses of this Psalm from the LXX are quoted by Paul in Romans 4:7-8 in
his example of David as a blessed man because his sin was forgiven.

Notice the different words used to describe rebellion against YHWH (cf. Ps. 32:5; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: FORGIVENESS IN THE OT).

- transgression – BDB 833, KB 981; it denotes an intentional breaking of that which
is God's will (i.e., covenant)

- sin – BDB 308, KB 306; it denotes missing (BDB 306) a set target, again not by ignorance
but willfully

- iniquity – BDB 730, KB 799; misdeed, guilt (#1,2,3 appear together in Exod. 34:7;
Lev. 16:21; Job 12:23; here; Isa. 59:12; Ezek. 21:24; Dan. 9:24)

- deceit – BDB 941, KB 636; means treachery, trickery, fraud (cf. Ps. 52:2; 101:7; 120:2-3)

The UBS Handbook mentions that the psalmist purposely alternated the
MASCULINE, FEMININE forms (twice) to show completeness (p. 303).

YHWH's (note the PASSIVE PARTICIPLES) forgiveness is described
as righteousness given to sinners based on God's mercy and their repentance (this is the theological
concept of imputed [cf. BDB 362, KB 359, Gen. 15:6; Rom. 4:3; Gal. 3:6]).

- forgiven (lit. "lifted and taken away") – BDB 669, KB 724, Qal
PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. Exod. 32:32; 34:7; Num. 14:18,19; Micah 7:18; same
word negated in Exod. 23:21; Josh. 24:19; Job 7:21; Isa. 2:9

- covered (i.e., puts out of sight, theological concept in Isa. 38:17; 43:25; Micah 7:19) –
BDB 491, KB 487, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE

The result is a person with no deceit/guile (cf. John 1:47). This does not
mean sinless, but repentant.

verses.zh: 凡心里没有诡诈、耶和华不算为有罪的，这人是有福的！
verses.en: How blessed is the one[NOTE:1] whose wrongdoing the Lord does not punish,[NOTE:2] in whose spirit there is no deceit.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “covered over.”

Heb “man.” The word choice reflects the perspective of the psalmist, who is male. The principle of the psalm is certainly applicable to all people, regardless of their gender or age. To facilitate modern application, the gender and age specific “man” has been translated with the more neutral “one.”
Heb “blessed [is] the man to whom the Lord does not impute wrongdoing.”
verses.commentary:
32:2 "man" This is the Hebrew word Adam (BDB 9). In the early parts of
Genesis (Genesis 1-3) it refers to Adam, the original human creation, but it took on the sense of
humanity in general (even Genesis 1-3).

▣ "spirit" See and
SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE.

verses.zh: 我闭口不认罪的时候，因终日唉哼而骨头枯干。
verses.en: When I refused to confess my sin,[NOTE:1] my whole body wasted away,[NOTE:2] while I groaned in pain all day long.
notes: In whose spirit there is no deceit. The point is not that the individual is sinless and pure. In this context, which focuses on confession and forgiveness of sin, the psalmist refers to one who refuses to deny or hide his sin, but instead honestly confesses it to God.
Heb “when I was silent.”
verses.commentary:
32:3-7 This strophe contrasts two ways to deal with sin.

- be silent, hide it

- bones wasted away, cf. Ps. 31:9-10

- groaning all day long

- vitality (lit. "juicy," BDB 545, cf. Num. 11:8; used here of body fluids)
drained away (NET Bible suggests an emendation to "to my destruction," p. 888 #29)

- man's needed response to sin

- I will acknowledge ‒ BDB 393. KB 390, Hiphil IMPERFECT

- I did not hide ‒ BDB 491, KB 487, Piel PERFECT

- I will confess ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a
COHORTATIVE sense

- YHWH's response to repentance

- YHWH forgives the guilt of sin (cf. Exod. 34:7; Num. 14:18; Ps. 85:2)

- sense of security returns

- YHWH is a hiding place again

- YHWH preserves him from trouble

- he is surrounded with songs of deliverance

There is a play on YHWH's hand.

- in judgment it was heavy (Ps. 32:4; Ps. 38:2; 39:10; Job 23:2)

- but in confession it protected him (Ps. 32:6-7)

verses.zh: 黑夜白日，你的手在我身上沉重；我的精液耗尽，如同夏天的干旱。（细拉）
verses.en: For day and night you tormented me;[NOTE:1] you tried to destroy me[NOTE:2] in the intense heat[NOTE:3] of summer.[NOTE:4] (Selah)
notes: Heb “my bones became brittle.” The psalmist pictures himself as aging and growing physically weak. Trying to cover up his sin brought severe physical consequences.
Heb “your hand was heavy upon me.”

You tried to destroy me. The psalmist’s statement reflects his perspective. As far as he was concerned, it seemed as if the Lord was trying to kill him.tc Heb “my [?] was turned.” The meaning of the Hebrew term לְשַׁד (leshad) is uncertain. A noun לָשָׁד (lashad, “cake”) is attested in Num 11:8, but it would make no sense to understand that word in this context. It is better to emend the form to לְשֻׁדִּי (leshuddi, “to my destruction”) and understand “your hand” as the subject of the verb “was turned.” In this case the text reads, “[your hand] was turned to my destruction.” In Lam 3:3 the author laments that God’s “hand” was “turned” (הָפַךְ, hafakh) against him in a hostile sense.
The translation assumes that the plural form indicates degree. If one understands the form as a true plural, then one might translate, “in the times of drought.”
verses.commentary: 32:4,5,7 "Selah" See note at Ps. 3:2 and Introduction to Psalms, VII.

verses.zh: 我向你陈明我的罪，不隐瞒我的恶。我说：我要向耶和华承认我的过犯，你就赦免我的罪恶。（细拉）
verses.en: Then I confessed my sin;I no longer covered up my wrongdoing.I said, “I will confess[NOTE:1] my rebellious acts to the Lord.”And then you forgave my sins.[NOTE:2] (Selah)
notes: Summer. Perhaps the psalmist suffered during the hot season and perceived the very weather as being an instrument of divine judgment. Another option is that he compares his time of suffering to the uncomfortable and oppressive heat of summer.
The Hiphil of ידה normally means “give thanks, praise,” but here, as in Prov 28:13, it means “confess.”
verses.commentary:
32:5 "I will confess" The parallelism of lines 1 and 2 demands a rare meaning
of the VERB (BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERFECT used
in a COHORTATIVVE sense). Usually the VERB in Hiphil
means "thanksgiving," but in a few contexts "confess" is the apparent meaning.

- 1 Kgs. 8:33,35; 2 Chr. 6:24,26 it denotes "confess YHWH's name"

- here and in Prov. 28:13 the context implies "confess sin"

verses.zh: 为此，凡虔诚人都当趁你可寻找的时候祷告你；大水泛溢的时候，必不能到他那里。
verses.en: For this reason every one of your faithful followers[NOTE:1] should pray to youwhile there is a window of opportunity.[NOTE:2] Certainly[NOTE:3] when the surging water[NOTE:4] rises,it will not reach them.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the wrongdoing of my sin.” By joining synonyms for “sin” in this way, the psalmist may be emphasizing the degree of his wrongdoing.
A “faithful follower” (חָסִיד, khasid) is one who does what is right in God’s eyes and remains faithful to God (see Pss 4:3; 12:1; 18:25; 31:23; 37:28; 86:2; 97:10).

Heb “at a time of finding.” This may mean, “while there is time to ‘find’ [the Lord]” and seek his forgiveness (cf. NIV). Some emend the text by combining מְצֹא (metsoʾ, “finding”) with the following term רַק (raq, “only, surely”) and read either ר[וֹ]מָצ (matsor, “distress”; see Ps 31:22) or ק[וֹ]מָצ (matsoq, “hardship”; see Ps 119:143). In this case, one may translate “in a time of distress/hardship” (cf. NEB, NRSV).
The Hebrew term רַק (raq) occasionally has an asseverative force.
The surging water is here a metaphor for trouble that endangers one’s life.
verses.commentary:
32:6 "in a time when You may be found" This ambiguous phrase can be understood in several ways.

- there is an appointed/appropriate time for repentance (LXX, Vulgate, NKJV)

- pray in time of need or distress (cf. 2 Chr. 15:4; emendation cf. NRSV, TEV, NJB)

- MT has "at a time of finding" (cf. Ps. 103:8-14; Isa. 55:6). JPSOA translates
this as "upon discovering [his sin]."

- also see Ps. 69:13; Isa. 49:8; 2 Cor. 6:2

The acceptable time is when the Spirit denotes YHWH's personal presence. We
can not choose "the acceptable" time. Humans are responders, not initiators in the spiritual realm.

▣ "in a flood of great waters" Water, raging water, is often used as an
idiom of trouble/distress/attack (cf. Ps. 69:1; 124:5; 144:7 and most beautifully in Isa. 43:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WATERS

verses.zh: 你是我藏身之处；你必保佑我脱离苦难，以得救的乐歌四面环绕我。（细拉）
verses.en: You are my hiding place;you protect me from distress.You surround me with shouts of joy from those celebrating deliverance.[NOTE:1] (Selah)
notes: Heb “him.” The translation uses the plural “them” to agree with the plural “every one of your faithful followers” in the first line of v. 6.
verses.commentary: 32:7 This refers to the tabernacle/temple. The songs of praise are worship songs or liturgy.

verses.zh: 我要教导你，指示你当行的路；我要定睛在你身上劝戒你。
verses.en: I will instruct and teach you[NOTE:1] about how you should live.[NOTE:2] I will advise you as I look you in the eye.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[with] shouts of joy of deliverance you surround me.”

The second person pronominal forms in this verse are singular. The psalmist addresses each member of his audience individually (see also the note on the word “eye” in the next line). A less likely option (but one which is commonly understood) is that the Lord addresses the psalmist in vv. 8-9 (cf. NASB “I will instruct you and teach you…I will counsel you with My eye upon you”).
Heb “I will instruct you and I will teach you in the way [in] which you should walk.”
verses.commentary:
32:8-11 The psalmist speaks to himself (and others, Ps. 32:5) on YHWH's behalf. Here is the
divine response, Ps. 32:8 (three COHORTATIVES)!

- Ps. 32:8, I will instruct you ‒ BDB 968, KB 1328, Hiphil IMPERFECT
used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I will teach you ‒ BDB 434, KB 436, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in a
COHORTATIVE sense

- I will counsel you ‒ BDB 419, KB 421, Qal COHORTATIVE, cf. Ps. 16:7

32:8 "in the way" This is an idiom for a godly life (cf. Ps. 1:1; 25:8-9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "with My eye upon you" This is an idiom of personal care and presence
(cf. Ps. 32:18; Ps. 34:15 [quoted in 1 Pet. 3:12]; Job 36:7).

For "eye" used of YHWH see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (ANTHROPOMORPHISM).

verses.zh: 你不可像那无知的骡马，必用嚼环辔头勒住它；不然，就不能驯服。
verses.en: Do not be[NOTE:1] like an unintelligent horse or mule,[NOTE:2] which will not obey youunless they are controlled by a bridle and bit.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “I will advise, upon you my eye,” that is, “I will offer advice [with] my eye upon you.” In 2 Chr 20:12 the statement “our eye is upon you” means that the speakers are looking to the Lord for intervention. Here the expression “my eye upon you” may simply mean that the psalmist will teach his pupils directly and personally.
The verb form is plural (i.e., “do not all of you be”); the psalmist addresses the whole group.
Heb “like a horse, like a mule without understanding.”
verses.commentary:
32:9 The person (PLURAL) who will not repent is described in terms of rebellious,
domesticated animals (cf. Isa. 1:2-3). Fallen humanity lives on an animal level characterized by
"more and more for me at any cost!"

▣

NASB, NKJV, LXX
"Otherwise they will not come near to you"

NRSV
"else it will not stay near you"

NJB
"there is no means of bringing them near"

REB
"so that they do not come near you"

Peshitta
"no one goes near them"

JPSOA
"far be it from you!"

This phrase is uncertain in the MT. Most translations think it refers to the
animals, but JPSOA, following Ibn Ezra, takes it as an admonition to faithful followers.

verses.zh: 恶人必多受苦楚；惟独倚靠耶和华的必有慈爱四面环绕他。
verses.en: An evil person suffers much pain,[NOTE:1] but the Lord’s faithfulness overwhelms the one who trusts in him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “with a bridle and bit, its [?] to hold, not to come near to you.” The meaning of the Hebrew noun עֲדִי (ʿadiy) is uncertain. Normally the word refers to “jewelry,” so some suggest the meaning “trappings” here (cf. NASB). Some emend the form to לְחֵיהֶם (lekhehem, “their jawbones”) but it is difficult to see how the present Hebrew text, even if defective, could have derived from this proposed original reading. P. C. Craigie (Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 265) takes the form from an Arabic root and translates “whose gallop.” Cf. also NRSV “whose temper must be curbed.”
Heb “many [are the] pains of evil [one].” The singular form is representative here; the typical evildoer, representative of the larger group of wicked people, is in view.
verses.commentary:
32:10 "lovingkindness" See
SPECIAL
TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (HESED).

▣ "shall surround" This VERB (BDB 685, KB 738, Poel
IMPERFECT) is also used in Ps. 32:7 of songs of deliverance and here of YHWH's
lovingkindness (cf. Ps. 32:10; also note Deut. 32:10; the ADJECTIVE is used in Ps. 34:7; 125:2).
What a wonderful idiom of YHWH's presence and protection!

▣ Again a contrast.

- the wicked – many sorrows

- the faithful follower (i.e., "he who trusts YHWH"), covenant loyalty and love
will surround him (cf. Ps. 32:7b, 10b, not "terror," Ps. 31:13).

verses.zh: 你们义人应当靠耶和华欢喜快乐；你们心里正直的人都当欢呼。
verses.en: Rejoice in the Lord and be happy, you who are godly!Shout for joy, all you who are morally upright![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “but the one who trusts in the Lord, faithfulness surrounds him.”
verses.commentary:
32:11 A series of PLURAL IMPERATIVES instructing the faithful follower.

- be glad – BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal IMPERATIVE

- rejoice – BDB 162, KB 189, Qal IMPERATIVE

- shout for joy – BDB 943, KB 1247, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

A life of joy amidst a fallen, unhappy world, is a powerful witness of God's presence
and character.

- How are Psalm 32 and 51 related?

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Because of the MT introduction many scholars believe this Psalm, like Psalm 51, describes
David's sin

- sexual encounter with Bathsheba

- murder of Uriah, cf. 2 Samuel 11

- cover up, cf. 2 Samuel 12

- forgiveness (i.e., although the consequences of his sin destroyed his family)

- in Rom. 4:7-8 Paul quotes 32:1-2 (LXX) as referring to David.

The supersciptions in the MT are not original, and thereby, not inspired. For a
full note, see Introduction to the Psalms, IV. Authorship

The term "maskil" (BDB 968, KB 641) is found in the superscriptions of several
Psalms. It's meaning is uncertain, but it relates to some type of poem put to music.

- David's sin is surely possible but it may have a wider implication and purpose (cf. PLURALS
of Ps. 32:11). Sin and its consequences are common to all humans (cf. Rom. 1:8-3:18,23), even
covenant humans (cf. Romans 7; 1 John 1:5-10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

- The psalmist's physical problems were surprisingly the merciful acts of God who would not allow the
sinful covenant person to remain in his/her rebellion (cf. Heb. 12:7-13). There are
consequences to sin, thank God, the God of mercy pursues us in spite of them. As sin
abounds, grace does much more abound (cf. Rom. 5:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

- One can tell which concepts, events, and issues are central to a culture by the number of
words used to describe it. Obviously Israel was concerned with covenant rebellion
(cf. 1 Kings 8), as well as its forgiveness. Hebrew has many words for sin and rebellion.

- Psalm 31 and Psalm 32 may have been placed together by an editor or compiler, because they
both discuss the physical results of sin (cf. Ps. 31:9-10; 32:3-4).

- The NASB Study Bible (p. 769) gives an interesting theory about the speakers.

- dialogue between David and YHWH in the tabernacle, Ps. 32:1-2

- David speaks to YHWH in the hearing of the gathered worshipers, Ps. 32:3-7

- a priest addresses David on YHWH's behalf, Ps. 32:8-10

- David speaks to the gathered worshipers, Ps. 32:11

- This Psalm emphasizes

- the sinfulness of humans

- the merciful character of God

- how a sinful human can become acceptable to a holy God (i.e., confession)

Paul's use of Ps. 32:1-2 in Romans 4, where he discusses OT
examples of "justification by grace through faith" (cf. Rom. 3:21-31;
Galatians 3; Eph. 2:8-9), reveals the context as an OT example of the theme developed
and prioritized in the NT. This is the heart of how one is forgiven, although the
mechanism for that forgiveness (i.e., the gospel of Christ) is not mentioned. It
still clearly reveals the merciful, gracious availability of YHWH's forgiveness
(i.e., "lifted and removed" and "covered").

If YHWH can forgive David, He can forgive you! Receive it through
confession and repentance! Then stand forgiven in the promises!
